subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should browser interactions make compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals the default model-facing contract, or keep the current capped snapshot behavior with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: Current code already has caps, efficient mode, and generic context guards, but the requested remaining change affects model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with full snapshot workflows.

options.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
options.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

options.title: Keep capped snapshots as default
options.body: Retain the current 40,000-character AI snapshot cap plus opt-in efficient mode and treat further compaction as targeted future work.

options.title: Route to broader context architecture
options.body: Track this under a larger tool-output/context compaction design if maintainers do not want a browser-specific default contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser snapshot default mode, bundled browser plugin ownership, and explicit-AI compatibility history make this the strongest routing candidate for the product-contract choice.
